explanation: Compared against Written on the Wall II (archived all.html and the definitions file wowIIdefs.js from cms.uhd.edu/faculty/delavinae/research/wowII/, via the Wayback Machine; the live site does not respond), Conjecture 181 (listed as open, Aug 8, 2005): 'If G is a simple connected graph on at least 2 vertices, then L_s(G) + b(G) ≥ α(G) + deg_avg(B(G^2))'. The Lean declaration is the negation of the universal statement Ls G + b G ≥ indepNum G + squarePeripheryAverage G, where squarePeripheryAverage is the average, over the vertices of maximum eccentricity of G², of their degree in G². I verified the cited counterexample T(7) = L(K_7) by hand: n = 21; a connected dominating set of the line graph is a connected edge set of K_7 whose vertices cover all edges, so it spans ≥ 6 vertices and has ≥ 5 edges, giving L_s = 21 − 5 = 16; an induced bipartite subgraph corresponds to an edge set of K_7 with maximum degree ≤ 2 and no odd cycle, so b = 6; α = 3 (a maximum matching of K_7); the graph has diameter 2, so G² = K_21, every vertex is peripheral in G² and has G²-degree 20. The inequality would read 22 ≥ 23, so the Lean statement is true. Interpretive caveat (hence severity 2): the source notation deg_avg(B(G^2)) does not say in which graph the degrees are taken. Reading it as the invariant 'average degree of the boundary' evaluated on the graph G² (as the Lean does) is consistent with the neighbouring conjectures 182–186 (Δ(G^2), rad(G^2), dist_avg(B(G^2),V(G^2)), ...), but WOWII's general definition of degree statistics over a vertex subset uses deg_G; under that alternative reading T(7) is not a counterexample (22 ≥ 3 + 10), so the 'solved, false' status depends on the chosen interpretation, which the docstring states only implicitly through its definition. Minor: the question tag is used although the source states a conjecture.
